lesson.title: Ik Zou Graag…
lesson.subtitle: polite requests and hypotheticals with zou

hook.title: Soften the Request
hook.content: Zou is the polite conditional: ik zou graag komen, zou u kunnen gaan? It turns a demand into a possibility. The infinitive still waits at the end.

pattern.title: Zou + infinitive, graag for politeness
pattern.content: Ik zou graag komen, ik zou willen werken, zou u kunnen gaan? The finite zou takes second place; the infinitive closes the sentence. Graag adds the polite 'gladly'.
pattern.trap_note: Zou is not the past of gaan. The past of gaan is ging; zou is the conditional of zullen.

exercises.prompt: Match each English meaning with its Dutch twin (Ik Zou Graag…):
exercises.target_answer: zou, willen, kunnen, graag, komen, gaan
exercises.meaning: would, to want, to be able to, gladly; please, to come, to go
exercises.explanation: These are the anchors of "Ik Zou Graag…": read each Dutch form through the pattern, not as a new word.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence says: “I would like to come.”?
exercises.explanation: “Ik zou graag komen.” is the Dutch form; the other readings bend the pattern of “Ik Zou Graag…”.

cues: The pattern: Zou + infinitive, graag for politeness
exercises.explanation: “Zou u kunnen gaan?” puts the thought together the Dutch way — Zou + infinitive, graag for politeness.

diagnosis.slip: an English-shaped word order slipped in
diagnosis.cue: Zou is not the past of gaan. The past of gaan is ging; zou is the conditional of zullen.

exercises.prompt: Which English sentence is built the Dutch way?
exercises.explanation: “Ik zou willen werken.” is word-for-word “I would want to work.”. The odd English is the lesson — never a model to produce. Pattern: Zou + infinitive, graag for politeness.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
cues: It means: We would like to eat.
exercises.explanation: “Wij zouden graag eten.” reuses only material taught in “Ik Zou Graag…” — Zou + infinitive, graag for politeness.
exercises.affirmation: You heard “Wij zouden graag eten.” — a sentence built from the lesson's own Dutch, practising Zou + infinitive, graag for politeness.

twist.prompt: One more, no safety net — say: “I would like to pay.”
twist.explanation: Zou + graag + infinitive is the polite request frame.

summary.outcome: Make polite requests and hypotheticals with zou.
summary.takeaway: Politeness is a modal stance; the bracket does not change.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on De Brug: Honger, Dorst & Leeftijd.

zou.etymology_derivation: The past form of zullen, used for polite conditionals.

willen.etymology_derivation: English will (as desire) and Dutch willen are the same verb.

kunnen.etymology_derivation: English can and Dutch kunnen are the same modal root.

graag.etymology_derivation: The adverb of willingness; Dutch uses it where English says 'like to'.

komen.etymology_derivation: English come and Dutch komen are the same verb; the vowel differs.

gaan.etymology_derivation: The same verb as English go, with the old g still pronounced.
